detail.longDescription: I have a generic event base where the discriminator is a type parameter so subclasses don’t redeclare kind : from typing import Annotated, Generic, Literal, TypeVar, Union from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, TypeAdapter K = TypeVar("K", bound=str) T = TypeVar("T") class Event(BaseModel, Generic[K, T]): kind: K data: T class Click(BaseModel): x: int y: int class Key(BaseModel): code: str class ClickEvent(Event[Literal["click"], Click]): pass class KeyEvent(Event[Literal["key"], Key]): pass AnyEvent = Annotated[Union[ClickEvent, KeyEvent], Field(discriminator="kind")] print(TypeAdapter(AnyEvent).validate_python({"kind": "key", "data": {"code": "Enter"}})) print(ClickEvent(data={"x": 1, "y": 2})) Validating through the union works: kind='key' data=Key(code='Enter') Constructing the subclass directly fails: Exit code 1 pydantic 2.13.5 pydantic_core 2.46.5 kind='key' data=Key(code='Enter') Traceback (most recent call last): File "/tmp/t.py", line 24, in <module> print(ClickEvent(data={"x": 1, "y": 2})) ~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/usr/local/lib/python3.13/dist-packages/pydantic/main.py", line 263, in __init__ validated_self = self.__pydantic_validator__.validate_python(data, self_instance=self) pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for ClickEvent kind Field required [type=missing, input_value={'data': {'x': 1, 'y': 2}}, input_type=dict] For further information visit https://errors.pydantic.dev/2.13/v/missing kind can only be "click" so I expect pydantic to fill it in. The only fix I found is redeclaring kind: Literal["click"] = "click" in every subclass, which is what the generic was meant to avoid. This works but it mutates model_fields and forces a rebuild: @classmethod def __pydantic_init_subclass__(cls, **kw): super().__pydantic_init_subclass__(**kw) args = get_args(cls.model_fields["kind"].annotation) if args: cls.model_fields["kind"].default = args[0] cls.model_rebuild(force=True) Is there a supported way to derive a field default from a Literal type argument or is redeclaring it per subclass the intended pattern?
